old.label: ImmunoXXL
old.arms: Prospective phase II · 16 of 61 atezolizumab–bevacizumab responders
old.result: Selected recipient subset: 2-y OS 94% from listing; death-censored recurrence-free estimate 90%; rejection 4/16 (25%); retransplant 2/16
old.caution: 16 selected from 61 treated; no ITT benefit or safe ICI washout established; short follow-up
quotes: Prospective single-centre observational cohort: 61 potentially eligible patients treated with atezolizumab–bevacizumab; 16 selected responders were enrolled, listed and transplanted.

Among 45 not included, 25 discontinued treatment (15 progression, four adverse events, six decompensation) and 20 failed downstaging criteria. Eight of 16 had baseline portal-vein tumor thrombosis (six Vp2, one Vp3, one Vp4); 15 had prior locoregional treatment. These were selected research recipients, not proof of standard eligibility after vascular invasion.

Median washout 57.5 days (IQR 29–87), median follow-up 16 months. Four biopsy-confirmed acute rejections (25%); three irAEs. Ninety-day morbidity 10/16 and mortality 1/16; two retransplants. Explants: ten complete and six partial responses; one recurrence. Reported two-year OS 94% (95% CI 67–100) and recurrence-free estimate 90% (62–98) in the 16 recipients; Methods start both clocks at listing and censor death for recurrence, so the latter is not conventional recurrence-or-death RFS.

Selected-16 outcomes, not efficacy among all 61 treated patients. Small, observational cohort with short follow-up. A shorter median washout does not establish safety. The fatal course included graft dysfunction, rejection, sepsis and retransplantation; graft loss should not all be attributed to rejection. Supplement and mechanistic analyses were not fully reviewed.
J Hepatol2026;85:117–129. PMID41763363. PDF pp3–5 selection, flow and endpoint definitions; Figures1–3; p8 safety; Table2. Targeted main clinical read; supplement not reviewed.
